thread:
nina: Heads up — I noticed some weird failures in the onboarding repo after the exports-map tidy in @redwood/sdk@0.8.0. Not just Cloudflare/Worker import errors — our internal publish script (monorepo pnpm pack step) started producing packages without the cjs entry.

omar: Can you paste the failure? Is this the same "no default export" issue?

nina: Slightly different. Pack log: `warning: package '@redwood/sdk' has no exports defined for require()`. Then downstream `pnpm` consumer (examples/cli) throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` when it does `require('@redwood/sdk')` in a legacy setup.

yuki: Ah yea, pack+exports interactions are nasty: our pack pipeline uses rollup to produce dist and then `pnpm pack` takes package.json's exports. Since we removed the "require" subpath in the exports map, pack produced an ESM-only tarball.

pat: Meanwhile customers on Dedicated with pinned Node 12/14 runtime are hitting CI too — their integration tests rely on `require('@redwood/sdk')` in some fixtures. This is bigger than onboarding samples.

omar: Two things we need: (1) a small compatibility layer so require() continues to work; (2) ensure types reflect reality so TS users aren't misled. Also update our pack step to validate both import and require smoke.

yuki: I pushed a branch that adds a `cjs/` wrapper and updates package.json exports to include: "." : { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./cjs/index.js" }. The cjs index does `module.exports = require('../dist/esm').default || require('../dist/esm')`.

nina: Nice. Also noticed `types` in package.json points at `dist/types/index.d.ts` which only exports named symbols now. I added a tiny `types/cjs.d.ts` that re-exports and declares `export default` so `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'` keeps working for consumers.

pat: Can we add a CI gate in `ci/release.yml` that runs `node -e "console.log(require('@redwood/sdk'))"` and a worker-emulation import `node --input-type=module -e "import('@redwood/sdk').then(() => console.log('esm ok'))"` against the generated tarball before publish?
yuki: Yep, added that to the branch and a smoke test that runs examples in a headless wrangler worker emulator.

omar: Also double-check auth/retry middleware packages. Some integration tests do `const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk')` and then call `sdk.default.auth.retry()`. If the wrapper returns an object shape that differs, we might break the middleware.

nina: I updated the cjs shim to keep the `default` property and also set named properties on `module.exports` — basically `const esm = require('../dist/esm'); module.exports = esm.default || esm; Object.assign(module.exports, esm);`. That preserves both shapes.

release-bot: publish-bot: Canary `@redwood/sdk@0.8.1-canary.4` published (includes cjs shim, types compat, and CI smoke tests).

ci-bot: ci: running samples matrix (node12/14/16, worker emulation, auth matrix) against canary.

pat: After local smoke: canary fixes the PNPM pack issue and worker import. Leaving it in canary for a day then we'll cut 0.8.1 patch. Also adding a short note to CHANGELOG about exports map and compatibility guidance.

yuki: Filing a follow-up ISSUE - add release checklist step: "validate exports for require/import + headless worker" so we don't regress this when making future exports changes.

omar: Thanks — big win to catch this before customers notice. :+1:
